pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Our Vision
Believe. Care. Transform
At Churchfield, our vision is simple, powerful and deeply rooted in who we are:
This vision guides every moment of school life. It calls us to believe in ourselves, care for others and transform the world together.
We care deeply for one another.
Our Mission
Our mission is to create classrooms where children achieve more than they think possible. Adults are empowered and supported to reach their highest aspirations too, so that everyone in our community can live life in all its fullness (John 10:10).
We commit to developing motivated, resilient, thoughtful and compassionate young people who are ready to contribute positively to society and the lives of others.
Our Values
These values shape who we are, how we learn and how we live together at Churchfield.
How Then Shall We Live?
We seek to create an inclusive, loving culture rooted in Christian teaching while celebrating and welcoming families of all faiths and none.
Our ethos encourages us to:
We want every child to know they are loved, valued and capable of extraordinary things.
show understanding, acceptance and mutual respect
practise compassion, fairness and forgiveness
Our Approach to Learning
At Churchfield we are building a curriculum that:
We believe learning is learnable — and we teach children how to become lifelong, joyful, resilient learners.
connects learning to real-world issues and needs
uses rich, authentic experiences, fieldwork and enquiry
Care. Believe. Transform.
Transforming the Future – Growing Together
At Churchfield, we plant seeds of possibility. We nurture roots that grow deep and strong.
We watch children flourish into young people ready to believe, care and transform the world.

Class Organisation At Churchfield Church School
Class Structure Overview
Churchfield Church School is a 12‑class primary school with a mixed‑age structure in some year groups. This approach allows us to balance class sizes, support children’s social development, and deliver a carefully planned curriculum that ensures consistency for every child.
Reception – 2 Classes (Early Years Foundation Stage / EYFS)
Years 1 & 2 – 3 Mixed‑Age Classes (Key Stage 1)
Years 3 & 4 – 3 Mixed‑Age Classes (Key Stage 2)
Year 5 – 2 Classes (Key Stage 2)
Year 6 – 2 Classes (Key Stage 2)
Understanding Mixed‑Age Classes
Because some classes contain two year groups, your child may spend two consecutive years in the same classroom. This is a normal part of our structure and is fully supported by our curriculum design.
You can explore our curriculum intent and structure here: Churchfield Church School and Nursery - Curriculum Intent

pageCache.text:
Welcome
Welcome to Churchfield Church School and Nursery
Welcome from the Executive Headteacher
Welcome to our school community.
It is a joy and a privilege to serve as Executive Headteacher of Churchfield, a place where every child is known, valued, and encouraged to shine.
At Churchfield, our draft vision is simple yet transformative:
These values shape who we are and who we aspire to be. Rooted in our Christian foundation, we are inspired by the words of St Paul:
“Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for the Lord.” — Colossians 3:23
This reminds us that every act - every moment of learning, kindness, courage, and service - holds value and purpose. It encourages our whole community to give their best, grow in character, and live with hope.
We believe every child carries a unique spark. Our role is to nurture that spark so every pupil feels safe, loved, confident, and ready to shine their light in the world. Through curiosity, creativity, reflection, and compassion, we help children become not just successful learners, but generous, thoughtful, and resilient people.
Churchfield is more than a school - it is a family.
A place where we “live life to the full” together.
Thank you for visiting our website. I hope it gives you a sense of the joy, warmth, and ambition that define our community. We would be delighted to welcome you further.
Jo Thorn Executive Headteacher

Believe in yourself.
Transform our world.

Wraparound Care (Reception - Year 6)
We provide wrap around care for as many children as require it in school. The provision is run by school support staff and based in Blossom class.
Breakfast club runs from 7.30 am - 8.40 am - this will cost £6.00 - all children will receive a breakfast.
After school club is available on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday 3 - 5pm & Friday 3 - 4pm
3.00 pm - 4.00 pm - £6.00
3.00 pm - 5.00 pm - £12.00
If you would like to book breakfast or afterschool club please log onto Arbor and you can select your choices under Clubs - please note 48 hours notice is required and you need to ensure there is money on the account prior to booking.
Please note: Late collections will incur an additional fee. Non payment of invoices will result in access to the provisions being refused.

pageCache.pageTitle: Churchfield Church School and Nursery - Maths

Maths
Maths at Churchfield
At Churchfield Church School, our aim is for every child to enjoy and be confident in maths so that they have the skills they will need to help them in later life. Our teaching follows the National Curriculum and we want children to be able to do these things:
Maths lessons In Reception, children have a short and interactive whole-class input every day. For example, they might be learning about how to identify one more or one fewer than a number. Reasoning and problem skills are developed alongside mathematical concepts. Children then access maths through their play both indoors and outdoors. Adults skilfully support children’s learning through play and small group teaching so that they meet their next steps.
Across Key Stages 1 and 2, we use a 'Spiral Curriculum' supported by White Rose resources. This curriculum design supports children's knowledge and retention by continually returning to key concepts to support memory in the most fundamental concepts. This is further supported by maths starters adapted to the needs of each class.
Children in Key Stages 1 and 2 have a daily lesson in maths. This consists of a range of whole-class teaching, group work guided by an adult and independent learning. Lessons provide children with opportunities to reason and problem solve. Planning for this is primarily supported by materials from National Centre for Excellence in Teaching Mathematics (NCETM) and White Rose Maths. Each lesson is used to make a small step in children’s understanding so that their understanding, skills and knowledge gradually gets stronger. In Key Stage 1, The Mastering Number programme is also used to consolidate children's understanding of number.

Music
Our vision for Music at Churchfield School
At Churchfield we understand the vital role music plays in supporting children’s emotional well being and developing confidence in an engaging, practical way. Music gives all children a “chance to shine”, take part and feel valued. At Churchfield we provide a rich curriculum of music activities that celebrates music throughout time and from many different cultures. Music is used to unite children (and the wider school community) bringing them together through song, performance and praise.
At Churchfield our music curriculum provides opportunities to
create music and compose.
learn and play unpitched and pitched instruments.
Take part in performance either as an ensemble or solo
Listen and appraise music from a wide range of genres
Go on educational visits to live performances that include a musical element.
Learn an instrument as an individual (paid for by parents)
Enjoy music based clubs such as choir.
By the time a child leaves Churchfield to attend secondary school they should be able to listen and appraise music using a range of musical instruments and voice. Children will have had the opportunity to sing in harmony and perform both voice and instrumental pieces. Children should have an understanding of the history of music and be able to talk about the features of music. Children will have been exposed to musical notation and should have some understanding of this.

pageCache.pageTitle: Churchfield Church School and Nursery - Attendance
pageCache.text:
Attendance
To report an absence: contact: Angela Fey
Telephone: 01278 782743
Email: office@churchfield.bwmat.org
We all know that when children are in school and are happy they learn best. This enables them to make progress and develop more within themselves. It is the aim of Churchfield Church School that pupils should enjoy learning, experience success and realise their full potential. Our Attendance Policy reflects this and recognises that regular attendance has a positive effect on the motivation and attainment of pupils.
We welcome children in from 8.40am where they can head to their classrooms and begin to enjoy their breakfast we provide (see breakfast section for details!). Registers are taken at 8.55am so we ask that all children are in their class and ready to learn by then so they can be marked on time. After this time they will be marked with a late code in the register. Gates will be closed at approximately 8.50am, so any children coming in this time will need to head through the main office and then into class. If it is after 9.15am your child will receive a unauthorised register code for being later after register closes and a valid reason must be provided or it will remain unauthorised.
All classes have the offer of a free breakfast (bagels, toast, cereal- sometimes even crumpets). This might be a second breakfast for some or a way of helping speed up the morning routine at home. We also run a paid breakfast club- contact the office for details.
If you know your child is going to be late or absent then please contact the school office as soon as possible. This should be done on a daily basis. Please do not wait for us to contact you as this reduces the time the admin team can spend on other duties and tasks.
While it is ultimately your responsibility as a parent/ carer to ensure your child's attendance, as a school team we want to work with families to support attendance as soon as possible. This can be through written communication or through meetings/phone calls to support you to help your children improve their attendance to help them learn more.
If you ever have any concerns around attendance or getting children into school in the morning please speak to the office to arrange a call back from the following staff.
Your child's class teacher in the first instance.
Family Support Workers- Elaine Tillam or Mandy Triggol
Ms Angela Fey for admin/ paperwork enquiries.
Mr M Kitchen - Assistant Head
Safeguarding and attendance are often linked so you might also want to speak to Mrs Claire Brewer our Safeguarding Officer.

Guidance for parents - Keeping your child safe online (1).docx Always be careful when you are using the internet. It can help you to keep in touch with your friends and help your education – but it can also cause harm – to you and to others.
Remember help is always available at school if you are having any problems online.
Don’t be afraid to talk to your teacher or another adult at school.
Information For Parents
Safer Internet Day: Parent/ child discussion
This discussion can be undertaken today or later in the week.
The Safer Internet day is aimed at children and young people aged 5 - 11 exploring what we can trust on the internet as part of our Safer Internet Day campaign.

pageCache.pageTitle: Churchfield Church School and Nursery - Severe Weather Procedure
pageCache.text:
Severe Weather Procedure
Should very severe weather conditions prevail, we would be grateful if parents/carers would observe the following procedure:
The school will remain open at all times and children will be expected to attend school unless:
School closures (somerset.gov.uk)
Parents/carers are expected to make themselves aware of school closure if it is clear that a closure is a possibility.
The school appreciates that during bad weather children may arrive later than normal; parents/carers should endeavour to contact the school to let them know they are on their way if likely to be delayed. The school recognises there will be isolated instances where families are cut off, even where the clear majority of children can get into school. In such instances parents/carers should inform the school of the circumstances of this exceptional situation, as the school has a duty to clarify the circumstances of each case so as to be able to formally authorise the absence to the Local Authority.
Where the school is officially closed, all pupil absence is counted as authorised absence.
During adverse weather conditions, only the main pedestrian entrance will be in use if the main playgrounds are out of use.
We will endeavour to make a decision about school closure as early in the day as practical, ideally at 7am. PLEASE DO NOT PHONE THE SCHOOL.
After a period of closure, a message will be sent to the parents/carers to advise them of the school’s reopening.
In the event of the school having to close during the day due to unforeseen worsening weather or similar unforeseen circumstances, parents/carers will be contacted by phone/message and asked to collect their child/ren. Such an early release will only be contemplated in very extreme circumstances. Children will not be sent home unless accompanied by a parent or adult nominated by a parent.
Every effort will be made to keep the school open and parents/carers should ensure that children should attend.
